turn_text: So Joyce, like your mother, you often say, don't find fault, find a way. Tell us about how that statement really turned into action in your life.

Well, it's interesting. And, you know, I talk about family and culture a lot because it's not unique to me, but for many individuals of my generation, and especially black Americans, we grew up in the community. It was the neighborhood. It was the church oftentimes, or the community center. But one thing my parents always said, because like all children, I was a normal kid. I complained a lot. I asked for things. I knew I wasn't going to get. And one day my mother sat me down and she said, you shouldn't ask for things or complain without resolve or an answer. And you know, that stuck with me. She said, one of the most profound gifts you can have is to think and create. She pushed us to read, to do well in school. And I was lucky or blessed or worked hard or a combination of that my grades were always excellent. But it was interesting that my mother would say, grades are grades, but what you make of yourself is how creative you are, how you can come up with your own answers.
